title-proc.eng: Provision of technical services for the AIDRA project demonstration on AI-enabled on-board data processing

description-proc.eng: The European Union Satellite Centre (SatCen) seeks to award a direct service contract to support the implementation of AIDRA (Artificial Intelligence In-orbit Data pRocessing Assessment), a cooperative initiative between the SatCen and the European Defence Agency (EDA). AIDRA is designed as a proof-of-concept to assess the feasibility, traceability, operational implications and governance conditions of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled On-Board Data Processing (OBDP) in support of Earth Observation (EO) and Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) workflows. The purpose of AIDRA is to generate independent, evidence-based insights into the maturity, risks and potential benefits of AI-OBDP for GEOINT, in support of EU objectives on technological readiness, operational effectiveness and secure information governance. The objective of the demonstration is to evaluate, under space-representative conditions, how AI-enabled on-board processing and tasking functions perform within an end-to-end EO data chain. The assessment focuses on technical behaviour, system performance and interaction with existing GEOINT workflow requirements. The initiative does not aim to deploy an operational capability, but to generate structured evidence to support institutional evaluation.

description-proc.fra: Le nouveau microscope à balayage électronique/à faisceau ionique focalisé par plasma qui doit être proposé sera utilisé aussi bien pour des applications en conditions cryogéniques (cryo ; matériaux biologiques congelés et échantillons sensibles issus de la science des matériaux, tels que les matériaux de batterie) qu'en conditions de température ambiante (tous types de matériaux). Ses principales applications seront la fabrication de lames pour TEM et de colonnes pour le synchrotron. Batteriematerialien) als auch bei Raumtemperatur (alle Arten von festem Material) verwendet werden. Das Gerät muss daher gleicherweise Raumtemperatur- und cryo-kompatibel sein, sowie ermöglichen, die Materialien unter Inertgas/Vakuum-Bedingungen zu transferieren. Bei den Hauptanwendungen handelt es sich um die Herstellung von dünnen Lamellen für die Untersuchung im Transmissions-Elektronenmikroskop und um die Herstellung von zylinderförmigen Proben für die Untersuchung mittels Röntgenstrahlung im Synchrotron. Weitere wichtige Anwendungen sind die Untersuchung von Materialoberflächen (inklusive mit dem Ionenstrahl hergestellte Querschnitte), die Herstellungen von 3D FIB-Tomogrammen und Prototyping. Die Möglichkeiten des Geräts sollen zudem durch ein Fluoreszenz-Lichtmikroskop und energiedispersive Röntgen-Spektroskopie ergänzt werden.
description-proc.eng: The new plasma-focused ion beam/scanning electron microscope to be offered will be shared for applications under cryogenic (frozen biological materials and battery materials) as well as under room temperature conditions (all types of materials). Its main applications will be the preparation of TEM lamellae and of pillars for X-ray investigations at the synchrotron. Material investigations (SEM imaging; FIB cross-sections), 3D FIB tomography and prototyping will be additional important topics. A fluorescence light microscope and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy will complement the capabilities of the instrument.

title-proc.eng: Micro-electrode array

description-proc.eng: The Drukker-Schröter group in the division of Cell Systems and Drug Safety at the Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research intends to purchase a multi-electrode array system for the assessment of electrical activity in specialized cell types differentiated from embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells. Research in our group is focused on the development of multicellular microphysiological models for target identification, drug discovery and safety testing. We develop these systems through the differentiation of embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells towards specialized cell types such as cardiomyocytes, neurons, and glia. An important aspect in our work is the molecular and functional characterisation of the cells that we differentiate. In the context of electrically active cell types, measurements of action potentials form an important aspect of this functional characterization. Multi-electrode arrays (MEAs) represent an accessible and scalable method to perform such functional characterisations, since they allow recording of electrical activity from several cells in a culture simultaneously, without laborious single cell-based interventions characteristic of more traditional electrophysiological assessment. This feature makes MEAs particularly suitable in the context of drug discovery and safety testing, where multiple conditions and cells need to be tested in parallel. This publication is to indicate our intention to award the contract to Maxwell Biosystems AG. If no representations are received within 20 days, we intend to award the contract.

title-proc.eng: 11835 - Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM)

description-proc.nld: The Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft, Faculty of Applied Sciences, has available funding through the Dutch Research Council (NWO) Knowledge and Innovation Covenant (KIC) consortium “Foundations for Electron-Beam Metrology and Inspection” for the acquisition of advanced electron microscopy instrumentation. The intended purchase is a high-end field-emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM) to support coherent diffractive imaging in both transmission and reflection geometries. The instrument must meet the following critical performance criteria: • High temporal and spatial coherence at acceleration voltages of 5–30 keV and probe currents of 25–100 pA. • Compatibility with bulk samples exceeding 70 × 70 mm, with multiple secondary and back-scattered electron detectors in reflection mode. • Stable stage and flexible chamber design to accommodate custom detectors and electro-optical components in reflection mode. • Support for direct-electron detectors in transmission (preferably retractable), with sufficient resolution inside the bright-field disk to enable diffractive imaging algorithms. This requires a large camera length and convergence angles exceeding 10 mrad at 30 keV. These specifications are essential to ensure the instrument can fully support the consortium research program in advanced electron-beam metrology and imaging. Motivation TU Delft has conducted an extensive market survey and technical evaluation of commercially available field-emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM) systems capable of meeting the functional requirements described above. Based on this assessment, TU Delft concludes that FEI Europe B.V. is currently the only supplier able to provide an instrument that meets the full combination of required specifications necessary for the successful execution of the intended research activities. On this basis, TU Delft intends to proceed with a single-supplier procurement procedure (see document).

title-proc.eng: Implementation of the Water Framework Directive - Policy Coherence, Managing Trade-Offs, Financing and Capacity

description-proc.eng: The objective of this research is to support the Forum to develop policy advice on the implementation of the 3rd cycle RBMP and development of the 4th plan. Learnings from the research are expected to inform Forum members about the existing obstacles in implementing the WFD in Ireland and to make recommendations about what can be strengthened going into the 4th cycle. In 2021, the Institute of Public Administration (IPA) assessed water governance in Ireland using the OECD Water Governance Indicator Framework to support the development of the third-cycle RBMP for Ireland 2022–2027. The primary objective of the Water Governance Indicator Framework (OECD, 2018) is to stimulate a transparent, neutral, open, inclusive and forward-looking dialogue across stakeholders on what does and does not work, what should be improved and who can do what. The IPA evaluated how Ireland was doing in relation to the 12 OCED principles of water governance, categorised each principle as “strong progress”, “good progress” or “limited progress”. In preparation for the development of the 4th cycle RBMP, the Water Forum is commissioning research to re-evaluate water governance around four OCED principles: 1. Policy coherence 2. Managing trade offs 3. Financing 4. Capacity Research Questions The Research should include an evaluation of how Ireland is doing in relation to the 4 OECD Principles below, identifying any relevant obstacles to implementation of the WFD in Ireland. Drawing on international case studies, the research should then present policy recommendations on how they could be strengthened going into the 4th cycle. 1. Policy Coherence • Review and evaluate policy coherence and cross-sectoral coordination which influence the implementation of the WFD, especially between policies for water and the environment, health, energy, agriculture, industry, spatial planning and land use. • Identify and evaluate the co-ordination mechanisms to facilitate coherent policies across ministries, public agencies and levels of government, including cross sectoral plans. • Identify and evaluate the barriers to policy coherence from practices, policies and regulations within and beyond the water sector.  Develop policy recommendations on how to strengthen policy coherence and cross sectoral coordination to support the implementation of the WFD in Ireland. 2. Managing Trade-offs • Review and evaluate how trade-offs are managed across water users, rural and urban areas and generations. • Review and evaluate how trade-offs are identified and communicated, and if efforts are made to minimise potential negative impacts on water.  Develop policy recommendations on how to improve the management of trade-offs to support the implementation of the WFD in Ireland. 3. Financing the WFD • Provide an overview on how the implementation of the WFD is financed in Ireland and evaluate if financial resources are allocated / used in an efficient, transparent and timely manner. • Identify financial / resourcing challenges which are impeding the implementation of the WFD in Ireland.  Drawing from international best practice or funding models to finance the WFD, develop policy recommendations on how to improve the financing of the WFD for strengthened implementation of the 4th RBMP. 4. Capacity • Provide an overview of the level of capacity both required and available to meet the complexity of meeting WFD objectives. • Identify capacity gaps which are impeding the implementation of the WFD in Ireland (e.g. policy, planning, project management, funding, scientists, advisory, monitoring, data, administration).  Develop recommendations on how to improve capacity to strengthen the implementation of the WFD in Ireland.

title-proc.eng: Delivery of Conservation Measures with a focus on control of Rhododendron in Twelve Bens/Garraun Plateau SAC , Mweelrea/Sheeffry/Erriff Complex SAC Maumturk Mountains SAC and the Connemara Bog Complex

description-proc.eng: This Call for Tender seeks a contractor to implement works as part of a multi-actor, community embedded ecosystem restoration programme. Building on pilot projects, 2021 to 2025, in Galway, Mayo, and Donegal, the contractor will focus on delivering peatland restoration whilst also building local capacity to address threats to peatland habitats, including Rhododendron ponticum, within the Connemara/SW Mayo region. Constructive engagement with farmers and landowners is a crucial element of this contract. Scope of work and deliverables The successful contractor will be responsible for delivering the following core pillars, Stakeholder Engagement and Capacity Building: Lead extensive formal and informal engagement with landowners, local authorities, NPWS and ACRES CP teams. This includes informing and engaging landowners, managing expressions of interest, EOIs, for peatland restoration, collaborating on a training programme for restoration methods, and upskilling personnel including farmers in the implementation of restoration actions, as appropriate. Surveying and Mapping: Complete comprehensive mapping of threats, invasive species, drainage, bare peat, across 15 high-priority sub catchments by 30th September 2026, see Appendix. This data will inform Site Specific Conservation Objectives, SSCOs, and blanket bog Provisional Restoration Requirements PRRs. PRRs are a new NPWS approach to identifying and prioritising areas with the highest restoration potential. Invasive Species Management: Implement Rhododendron control across c.300ha and re-treatment of c.190ha across the Twelve Bens, Connemara Bog, Mweelrea,Sheeffry,Erriff, and Maumturk Mountains SACs see Appendix.Peatland Restoration Planning: In partnership with LIFE IP Wild Atlantic Nature, oversee the restoration of c.70ha of blanket bog in Connemara following a detailed Restoration Action Plan. A draft Restoration Action Plan will be available to the successful contractor. Furthermore, the contractor will engage a hydro-ecologist or other suitably qualified person to develop three site-specific restoration plans covering c.250ha of blanket bog. Replacement of Rhododendron hedgerow: Manage a pilot scheme to replace Rhododendron hedgerows with native species and establish monitoring protocols for soil recovery in cleared areas. Tenderers should price for approximately 450m of hedgerow replacement. Communication, dissemination and networking: The successful tenderer will share information and findings from the project and engage in knowledge exchange with relevant stakeholders including other Natura Communities projects, Local Authorities, NPWS, FarmUP EIP, and others. This Call for Tender invites proposals from qualified contractors to further develop a multi-actor, community-led ecosystem restoration project, which is building on successful preliminary projects across Donegal, Mayo, and Galway refer to Appendix 5. Building on the foundational work established between 2021 and 2025, this contract focuses on scaling local capacity to execute restoration actions, primarily targeting Rhododendron ponticum control and broader peatland restoration. All actions must align with Site Specific Conservation Objectives SSCOs and address identified environmental pressures within the target areas. The successful tenderer will be responsible for: Convening and facilitating a Project Steering Group comprising relevant stakeholders and technical advisors. Appointing a dedicated Project Coordinator to manage the development and implementation of the Conservation Measures programme. Providing comprehensive technical and administrative support, including specialist ecological advice on Rhododendron management, GIS mapping, and the provision of all necessary training materials and equipment. Maintaining continuous engagement with local landowners and community actors to ensure transparency and maximise participation.

title-proc.eng: Multi Supplier Framework Agreement for the provision in four lots of Offshore Renewable Energy and Renewable Energy Consultancy RFT 233409 - (PAS126F) - Request for Tenders for Provision of – [Electricity Storage] Emerging Technology Sandbox – Strategic Analysis Report

description-proc.eng: In line with Climate Actions Plan actions (EL/23/23 & EL/24/16), in July 2024 the Electricity Storage Policy Framework (ESPF) for Ireland was published. The ESPF sets out the strategic role that electricity storage systems play in Ireland’s energy transition and the key role they will play in our zero-carbon future. It contains 10 Government actions to support the incorporation of electricity storage systems to the electricity grid network. Action #2 of the Electricity Storage Policy Framework: ‘Emerging Technology Sandbox’ (sandbox), actions the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment to establish a Sandbox project in conjunction with both the System Operators, EirGrid and ESB Networks. A ‘Sandbox’ is an environment in which technologies can be tested in isolation and thus allows for research into new and emerging technologies whilst preventing them from impacting the wider system in which they would operate, in this case the electricity grid network. The principal objective of the Sandbox is to increase the technological knowledge of the System Operators regarding the incorporation of new and emerging electricity storage technologies to the Irish grid system. Successful completion of this project will situate the Irish grid system and the System Operators in an advantageous and attractive position vis a vis the trialling and location of new and emerging electricity storage technologies, which in turn will accelerate the incorporation of new electricity storage technologies, capable of accelerating Irelands energy transition, on to the Irish grid network. A Strategic Analysis Report (SAR) is required to progress this government action.
